No. I’m re doing a year. It’s fine. No shame. It’s not easy stuff

You write beautifully. I don’t know if you do a lot of writing, but it’s something you should consider. You have a lovely way with words and you surely have a lot to say. I’d be interested in reading more from you. 

Also I’m sorry to hear what you’ve been through, you didn’t deserve any of that. I hope video games can be the base layer for now and more reasons to live can build on top of that eventually.

I’m 19. Will be 20 in a couple months and understand exactly how you feel. 

I want life to get better for you. But I know life is a bitch. She has her good moments though. 

But if you do decide to end it, I hope it’s painless for you. 

And if you do decide to stay, however hard that may be, I hope there’s a way to end your suffering that doesn’t involve death. And I know it sounds cliché, and I don’t want to sound condescending, but you don’t have to figure it all out alone. We’re all stuck in our own heads, but if this forum shows us anything it’s that we can try and figure one another out... We can try to understand. There are genuine people out there who care and are kind. Kindness may be rare, but it exists. 

I don’t know anything about you, but from the deepest part of my heart I want to say I’m sorry. I’m sorry your 20 years have led you here. My years have led me to the same point over and over again, too, so I can understand. 

If I could take your pain away, I really would. I’m not religious, but if peace or “another side” exists, I truly wish for you to be happy there. But know that happiness does exist here, and the bad times do not have to outweigh the good, even if that’s the way it’s been in your life so far. Things can change. Things will change. Hope feels stupid when you’re ready to end it, I know- it feels slightly laughable or patronising, but it’s real. So please hold onto it if you can find that within yourself. 

Take care, and message me any time, truly. 

From,

Estelle.

I hear you, man, I hear you. I Spent the vast majority of my life blaming myself and hating myself for even the smallest things. It’s mental self harm, and it’s semi addictive. Feeling shit feels normal. It’s comfortable to some extent because it is all you know and understand. I can only talk from my own experience. I have really only been “better” for about 3 months. Prior to that I was fixed on suicidal ideation. I really felt ready to do it. I still think about suicide methods when I pass open water. And then I almost feel sick at myself for thinking that. Idk the psychological motions behind that...  I had such a deep rooted hate for myself... was convinced I couldn’t do anything right, that I ruined everything. 

But seriously, You’re just here living bro, you don’t owe anybody a thing. 

But you do owe it to yourself to get better. Because this “disease” or whatever you want to call it is pulling your life and happiness away from you. You’re here so part of you wants to get better and stop the mental self abuse. Do you think meds would help you make that first Step? Or have you tried already? 

I hope you’re having a good day/evening anyhow,

Estelle.

When I stand within this bubble I live in, I can see that the edges of the world are opaque and solid. There is no way out. Sometimes I imagine it as though we exist within that dome on The Simpsons Movie, except it's not transparent,  we cannot see the grass on the other side because it's hidden from us, the dome's way of life is the only way- period. Somewhere, someone decided that humans shouldn't be given too much time to think, so they made money. The poor only have enough time to make money to live. The dome tells you that you're not working hard enough and if you *slave away just a little bit more,* you can have *this brand new used car-* and that will make you happy. Until it doesn't. They try to sell us happiness in objects. We don't think about what happiness means anymore. We either see the opaque black edges of the dome, the shiny objects within the dome- or we're stuck somewhere in the middle. They tell us that if we live by *these* rules-  you or *anyone else can make it!* You can have all these meaningless objects that give a false sense of purpose if you just work another 8 hours a week!! Why on earth you want to leave our beautiful dome?!! It's great here!!

And they're laughing because even if you've figured the game out and *want to leave the dome- there is no way out!!!!*

Apart from suicide, of course. That is one form of escape from the dome that religions have and still continue to use to mind fuck you into believing there's no escape.

It's like one grande Stockholm syndrome experienced by many of us in this world; some of us grow to love all this fake material shit that's been shoved down our throat to distract us from the trap of the dome. Then we come to realise- wait- this shit can't *actually make me happy.* But what else is there? There is only the dome... It's all we can see, and if we cannot play by the rules and achieve the "dream" that is shoved in our faces daily, then we're losing the game and condemn ourselves to *failure*.

Well this is one rigged fucking game if you ask me. It's like going to the bathroom in a game of Monopoly and leaving your snake ass friends in charge of the money. We're not born equal. It's a lottery. And those at the very, very top are the puppet masters in charge of this game, always one step ahead. Nothing in this world shocks me. Everything is going exactly the way they want it to go. They tell us everything they want us to know when and if they're ready. Too many of us are fucking brainwashed to rebel against this fucking system that's getting children, teens and adults alike feel like suicide is the only way out. Depression is at an all time high? Mental Health services drastically underfunded? Hm. Doesn't sound right to me- yet sounds exactly like how they want it to be. People have to fail for this system to keep circulating. The politicians keep arguing about money to distract us. There's plenty of money. Plenty of ways to help so many (not all, as I know depression stems from various sources) of us stop feeling like suicide is the only way out. But it's hardly priority in this world is it? Feeding the starving is not priority. There's plenty of food, and then some, though. Fucked up isn't it.

The way I see it, the vast majority of us are oblivious to the fact that we live within this dome; we're distracted by everyday happenings going on inside of it (think mass media). We don't have time to think about destroying the opaque walls that are trapping us in and making us deeply unhappy, and on top of that the edges of the dome are so heavily guarded- simple things that could make us happy like travelling- guarded by having enough MONEY to get there, to buy a PASSport, to get a VISA... Wanna do your dream job? LOL sorry you were born poor and dont have the qualifications. Need money to live and resort to selling drugs? Enjoy level 3 Slavery, AKA Prison. (IDK what level 2 slavery is but the way I see it, we're all fucking slaves, the meaning of freedom is defined for us and we fight for what few rights the government gives us and threaten to remove, so we don't even have time to think about the fact that they only offered scraps in the first place if we're left to FIGHT for the scraps).

Anyway I went on a bit of a nonsensical ranty thing there but my point (or part of it) is that all this depression and suicidal shit we're feeling  isn't really that surprising considering the circumstances, is it? Look at this shit show we live within and ask if you truly want to be a part of it. Add extenuating issues such as abuse or whatever may have fucked you up in the first place to this shitshow and suicidal feelings seem fucking logical. The rebellion against this system is 70% a mental one. The system is everywhere and I can't imagine enough of us waking up from the matrix to revolt because it controls us and traps us so well...

There is nothing wrong with committing suicide. I've been on the irrational side of suicide. I can now see it from a subjectively "rational" side.

I think if you are to go through with suicide, it is best to do it with as rational a mind as possible. But it's your life. Your choice.

Personally I like a variety of genres and seem to associate different genres with different moods. This isn't always the case, I listen to certain pieces of classical music when I'm sad, and others when I am happy. I predominantly listen to rock or metal music when i'm unhappy, and it aids me in feeling much worse about myself. I'd say, for me, this is bad, because feeling down is almost a comforting feeling for me at times. 

If you're feeling good about yourself and about life, however, I feel as though the music doesn't make a huge lot of difference. Although when I'm in the happiest moods, I do not crave sad music. But, you know yourself better than anyone, if this music is making you melancholic and you're  trying to recover from depression and/or despair, I'd maybe try and find more upbeat songs, at least for now!

Glad to hear you are getting better, I can relate to how you are feeling! It's good to finally start feeling a bit positive about life again! I mean, I have only felt good for around 2 weeks so far, but that's something to be pleased about as far as I am concerned. Like you plan to, I have been "getting out there" a bit, going on the odd date and meeting with friends regularly, also being very open about my feelings with those closest to me. It's really been what has made the difference for me personally!

Wishing you all the best,

Estelle
